누나.m: older sister (of a male); older female friend (of a male)
누나.x: My older sister works at a company.
누나.t: Only males say 누나. Females call an older sister 언니.

가끔.x: I sometimes go hiking on weekends.

잔돈.x: Sorry, I don't have any small change right now.
잔돈.e: 잔- 'small, fine' (as in 잔소리 'nagging') plus 돈 'money'.

하숙집.x: I lived in a boarding house during my freshman year of college.
하숙집.e: 하숙 (lodging with meals included) + native 집 (house).
하숙집.t: A 하숙집 usually includes home-cooked meals, which a 원룸 does not.

대화.x: I had a conversation in Korean with a Korean friend.

요새.x: I'm so busy these days because I have a lot of work.
요새.e: Short for 요사이 'this interval'; a different 요새 means 'fortress'.

응급실.ex: 밤에 배가 너무 아파서 응급실에 갔어요.
응급실.x: My stomach hurt so much at night that I went to the ER.
응급실.e: Literally 'room for responding to urgent cases.'
응급실.t: Pronounced [응급씰] — the ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

수리.x: The washing machine broke, so I sent it in for repair.

잎.x: This plant has very big leaves.
잎.e: Often combined as 나뭇잎 (tree leaf) and 꽃잎 (flower petal).
잎.t: 잎이 is pronounced [이피], but 잎 alone and before consonants sounds like [입].

안전벨트.x: Always fasten your seat belt when you get in the car.
안전벨트.t: You 매다 a seat belt (안전벨트를 매다) and 풀다 to unfasten it.

무시하다.m: to ignore, to disregard; to look down on
무시하다.e: Literally 'not look' — act as if you don't see it.
무시하다.t: It also means 'to look down on someone': 어리다고 무시하면 안 돼요.

유지하다.x: Keep the indoor temperature at 20 degrees.
유지하다.e: Literally 'tie and hold' — keep things as they are.

과연.m: indeed, just as expected; (in questions) I wonder if really
과연.ex: 과연 소문대로 이 식당 음식이 정말 맛있었어요.
과연.x: Just as people said, this restaurant's food really was delicious.
과연.e: Literally 'the result is so' — it turned out as predicted.
과연.t: In questions it expresses doubt: 과연 그게 가능할까요? 'Is that really possible, I wonder?'

이어지다.m: to continue, go on; to be connected, lead to
이어지다.x: The meeting went on until late at night.
이어지다.t: Also 'lead to': 작은 실수가 큰 사고로 이어질 수 있어요 'a small mistake can lead to an accident.'

부유하다.x: He was born into a wealthy family.
부유하다.t: Rather formal; in speech people usually say 부자예요 or 돈이 많아요.

부유하다.ex: 공기 중에 미세 먼지가 부유하고 있습니다.
부유하다.x: Fine dust is floating in the air.
부유하다.t: Homonym: the adjective 부유하다 means 'wealthy'; this verb is the scientific 'to float, drift'.

영향을 미치다.forms: N에 영향을 미치다 · 미쳐요 · 미쳤어요 · 미칠 거예요
영향을 미치다.m: to influence, to have an effect on
영향을 미치다.ex: 스마트폰은 아이들의 생활에 큰 영향을 미쳐요.
영향을 미치다.x: Smartphones have a big influence on children's lives.
영향을 미치다.e: 영향 is literally 'shadow and echo'; 미치다 here means 'to reach'.
영향을 미치다.t: This 미치다 'to reach' differs from 미치다 'to go crazy'; in casual speech, 영향을 주다 is more common.

완치.ex: 꾸준히 치료를 받으면 이 병은 완치될 수 있어요.
완치.x: With steady treatment, this disease can be completely cured.

금주.x: The doctor told me to quit drinking for my health.
금주.e: Literally 'forbid alcohol'. 금- = banning: 금연, 금지.
금주.t: Homonym: in formal writing 금주 can also mean 'this week.'

주연.ex: 그 배우가 처음으로 주연을 맡은 영화예요.
주연.x: This is the first movie in which that actor played the lead role.
주연.t: 주연 is the actor's position; 주인공 is the character in the story.

지구 온난화.ex: 지구 온난화 때문에 여름이 점점 더워지고 있어요.
지구 온난화.x: Summers are getting hotter and hotter because of global warming.

수사.x: The police are investigating the case.
수사.t: 수사 is a criminal investigation by police or prosecutors; 조사 is any examination, survey, or research.

허탈하다.m: drained, deflated, dejected (after effort comes to nothing)
허탈하다.ex: 열심히 준비한 행사가 취소되어서 정말 허탈했어요.
허탈하다.x: The event I'd worked so hard on was canceled, and I felt completely deflated.
허탈하다.e: Literally 'emptied out', as if all your strength has slipped away.

반환하다.m: to return, to give back, to refund
반환하다.x: When the contract ends, we'll return your deposit.

해제하다.m: to lift, to cancel, to release (a restriction, alarm)
해제하다.x: The typhoon passed, so the weather agency lifted the warning.
해제하다.t: Everyday use: 잠금을 해제하다 (unlock a phone), 알람을 해제하다.

배다.m: to soak in, permeate (smell, sweat); to become ingrained
배다.x: I grilled meat, and the smell soaked into my clothes.
배다.e: Homonym warning: another 배다 means 'to be pregnant with', as in 아이를 배다.
배다.t: 몸에 배다 means a habit has become second nature.

훈훈하다.x: Hearing that story warmed my heart.
훈훈하다.e: Sino-Korean: a doubled syllable meaning 'warm, fragrant', for gentle, lingering warmth; now also slang for 'good-looking' (훈남).

시점.x: It's hard to make a decision at this point.
시점.t: Homonym: 시점 meaning 'point of view' is used for narration, as in 1인칭 시점.

여지.ex: 그 문제는 아직 논의할 여지가 있어요.
여지.x: There's still room to discuss that issue.
여지.e: Literally 'leftover ground': space still left over.
여지.t: 의심의 여지가 없다 means 'there's no room for doubt.'

양극화.ex: 소득 양극화가 심각한 사회 문제가 되었어요.
양극화.x: Income polarization has become a serious social problem.
양극화.t: Pronounced [양그콰] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

논조.m: tone (of an argument or article), editorial line
논조.ex: 두 신문은 그 사건에 대해 논조가 완전히 달랐습니다.
논조.x: The two newspapers took completely different tones on the incident.

논거.ex: 그 주장을 뒷받침할 논거가 아직 부족해 보여요.
논거.x: There still doesn't seem to be enough evidence to back up that claim.
논거.t: Collocation: 논거를 제시하다 'present grounds'; 논거 is the evidence, 논증 the whole argument.

묘사.x: The author described the main character's psychology in fine detail.

분포하다.m: to be distributed, to be spread (over an area)
분포하다.ex: 이 식물은 주로 남부 지방에 분포합니다.
분포하다.x: This plant is mainly found in the southern regions.

가늠하다.m: to estimate, to gauge, to guess
가늠하다.ex: 피해 규모가 너무 커서 가늠하기조차 어려워요.
가늠하다.x: The scale of the damage is so large it's hard even to estimate.

유괴.ex: 부모들은 아이들에게 유괴 예방 교육을 시켜요.
유괴.x: Parents teach their children how to avoid being kidnapped.
유괴.e: Literally 'luring and tricking away' — taking someone by deception.
유괴.t: 유괴 usually implies tricking a child; 납치 is a broader word for taking someone by force.

서원.ex: 한국의 서원 아홉 곳이 세계유산으로 지정되었어요.
서원.x: Nine Korean seowon academies were designated as World Heritage sites.
서원.e: Literally 'book institution'; it combined a school with a shrine to scholars.
서원.t: Don't confuse it with 서당, a small village school where children learned basic characters.

패륜.m: gross immorality, violation of human morality (esp. toward family)
패륜.ex: 부모를 폭행한 패륜 사건이 뉴스에 보도되었습니다.
패륜.x: A shocking case of someone assaulting their parents was reported on the news.
패륜.t: A very strong word, typically for crimes against one's own family; 패륜아 is the person who commits them.

이단.ex: 중세 교회는 새로운 사상을 이단으로 몰기도 했어요.
이단.x: The medieval church sometimes branded new ideas as heresy.
이단.e: Literally 'a different end': straying from the main line.
이단.t: In Korea, 이단 often refers to controversial new religious groups that mainstream churches reject.

결벽증.m: mysophobia, compulsive cleanliness, being a neat freak
결벽증.ex: 제 룸메이트는 결벽증이 있어서 하루에 세 번 청소해요.
결벽증.x: My roommate is a neat freak and cleans three times a day.
결벽증.t: Very common in casual speech for a neat freak, not only a medical diagnosis.

사실주의.ex: 사실주의 소설은 평범한 사람들의 삶을 그대로 그립니다.
사실주의.x: Realist novels portray ordinary people's lives just as they are.
사실주의.e: -주의 = '-ism': 사실주의, 자본주의, 민주주의. 사실 is 'depicting the real.'
사실주의.t: This 사실 (寫實) is not 사실 (事實) 'fact' — same sound, different hanja.

필치.ex: 작가는 섬세한 필치로 시골 풍경을 그려 냈어요.
필치.x: The author depicted the countryside with a delicate touch.
필치.e: Literally 'brush manner' — the feel of someone's writing or brushstrokes.
필치.t: Usually adjective + 필치로: 섬세한 필치로, 담담한 필치로 '(written) in a delicate / calm style'.

외적 갈등.forms: 외적 갈등이 생기다 · 외적 갈등을 해결하다
외적 갈등.ex: 주인공과 사회 사이의 외적 갈등이 점점 커져요.
외적 갈등.x: The external conflict between the main character and society keeps growing.
외적 갈등.e: Literally 'outer conflict' — a character against other people, society or nature.

옴니버스.m: omnibus, anthology (film or book of separate stories)
옴니버스.ex: 이 영화는 세 감독이 함께 만든 옴니버스 영화예요.
옴니버스.x: This movie is an anthology film made by three directors.
옴니버스.e: From English 'omnibus' — in Korea it mostly means a film or drama of separate short stories.

사관.x: The view used to interpret history differs from era to era.
사관.e: Literally 'history view.' -관 = outlook: 역사관, 가치관, 세계관.
사관.t: 사관 also means 'court historian' or 'military officer' (different hanja); context decides.

관철하다.m: to carry through, to push through (a demand or will) to the end
관철하다.x: The union finally got its demands accepted.
관철하다.t: Common pattern: 요구를 관철하다 or 뜻을 관철하다, meaning to get one's way in the end.

일임하다.m: to entrust entirely, to leave (something) completely to someone
일임하다.x: We left all the decisions entirely to the team leader.
일임하다.e: Literally 'one entrusting' — handing over the whole thing.
일임하다.t: Pronounced [이림하다] — the ㄹ links to the next vowel.

기실.ex: 그는 강해 보이지만 기실 마음이 여린 사람이에요.
기실.x: He looks tough, but in fact he's a soft-hearted person.
기실.e: Literally 'its truth': the real fact behind appearances.
기실.t: Very literary; in speech, say 사실은 or 실은.

기부문화.ex: 연말이 되면 기부문화를 확산하자는 캠페인이 많아요.
기부문화.x: At the end of the year there are many campaigns to spread a culture of giving.

북돋우다.x: The coach tried to boost the players' morale.
북돋우다.e: 북 (soil heaped around a plant's roots) + 돋우다 (to raise): helping a plant grow.

삼엄하다.ex: 정상 회담장 주변은 경비가 매우 삼엄했습니다.
삼엄하다.x: Security around the summit venue was extremely tight.
삼엄하다.e: Literally 'dense and strict', like a forest of guards.
삼엄하다.t: Classic news collocation: 경비가 삼엄하다 'security is tight'.

절절하다.ex: 편지에는 고향을 그리는 마음이 절절하게 담겨 있었어요.
절절하다.x: The letter was filled with a heartfelt longing for home.

초롱초롱하다.x: The child looked up at me with sparkling eyes.

귀추.x: All eyes are on how these negotiations will turn out.
귀추.t: Almost always in the news phrase 귀추가 주목되다 'all eyes are on the outcome'.

모태.ex: 이 작은 모임이 지금 회사의 모태가 되었어요.
모태.x: This small group became the origin of the current company.
모태.t: Fun collocations: 모태 신앙 'faith from birth', slang 모태 솔로 'never dated'.

탈피.x: We need to break away from outdated ways of thinking.
탈피.e: Literally 'shedding skin', like a snake molting.
탈피.t: Pattern: N에서 탈피하다, 'to break out of N.'

효시.m: beginning, forerunner, the first of its kind
효시.ex: 이 소설은 한국 현대 소설의 효시로 평가받아요.
효시.x: This novel is regarded as the forerunner of modern Korean fiction.
효시.e: Literally 'whistling arrow', once shot to signal the start of a battle.
효시.t: Pattern: N의 효시로 꼽히다/평가받다, 'to be considered the first N.'
